items.title: AFL matriarch stored guns for Dezi Freeman, helped wife get to Australia
items.description: Kay Reid, the mother of premiership players Ben and Sam Reid, reveals that she and her husband Bruce's deep ties to the dead fugitive and his family date back two decades.

items.title: Oil flows through strait but Lebanon strikes raise peace doubts
items.description: Some 12.5 million barrels of crude oil have sailed through the Strait of Hormuz overnight, US Vice President JD Vance says, but in Lebanon, Israel launched fresh air strikes, raising doubts over peace in the region.

items.title: Zelenskyy warns 'Moscow will burn' as Russian capital comes under attack
items.description: Scores of drones targeted Moscow overnight in what was Ukraine's largest attack on the Russian capital.

items.title: Albanese government finds itself in policy quicksand on three core issues
items.description: The government's announced changes to its tax package are seeking to allay the fierce post-budget backlash from vested interests and some commentators.

items.title: Global telco escapes penalty for bank scam texts despite customers losing millions
items.description: A global telco that failed to stop more than 1,000 scam text messages from reaching Australians has faced no consequences, the ABC can reveal.

items.title: Hanson's 'scary' parental leave views outdated, advocates say
items.description: Pauline Hanson's openness to discuss a winding back of paid parental leave is concerning and harks back to an Australia that no longer exists, advocates say.

items.title: Live: Treasurer says Labor has lost 'political paint' from budget as he defends backdown
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says the federal government has lost "political paint" from May's budget while defending a backdown on key budget measures. Follow live.

items.title: The pros and cons of retiring overseas with your pension
items.description: With some foreign countries offering cheaper living expenses, it is no surprise that moving overseas to retire is increasingly attractive to some older Australians. But before you up stumps and book that flight, read this.

items.title: Live: Five goals and red card spark Swiss delight, American star in doubt for Socceroos clash
items.description: Switzerland beats 10-man Bosnia and Herzegovina 4-1 in a flurry of late drama, while US talisman Christian Pulisic doesn't train ahead of his side's clash with the Socceroos. Follow live.

items.title: New data shines light on state of EV public charger network
items.description: It's often claimed Australia has an EV public charger shortage, but analysis of exclusive data shows most fast charger sites are not congested.

items.title: Man arrested after boy critically injured in crocodile enclosure at UK zoo
items.description: British police say they have arrested a man on suspicion of attempted murder after being called to a popular zoo north of London.

items.title: Democrats chewing nails as Trump targets controversial Senate pick
items.description: A Democrat is accused of being a Republican in disguise; a Republican is accused of being a Democrat plant. It's primaries season in the US, and suspicions of dirty pool are rife.

items.title: 'Sleepwalking into a catastrophe': Proposed data centre raises water fears
items.description: To its supporters, this proposed data centre will provide much-needed regional jobs, but in the nation's driest state, critics say the draw on river water to cool the machines could be too great.

items.title: Crows legend Tony Modra seriously injured in crash
items.description: Crows legend Tony Modra has been seriously injured in a truck crash.

items.title: Would you live in a 1930s pump station? This couple made one their home
items.description: From former post offices to pumping stations, there are buildings with commercial histories all around Australia. Could repurposing them into homes help with the housing supply?

items.title: Friday news quiz: Soccer celebrations, bin battles, phone fails and an internet-famous duck
items.description: Today's news quiz is heating up like El Niño. Will you strut like an internet-famous duck or get schooled like Prince George?

items.title: No princesses, no musical numbers: How Toy Story changed children's cinema
items.description: The multi-billion-dollar franchise has overcome rewrites, accidental deletions and generations of changing tastes to bring Toy Story 5 to cinemas in 2026.

items.title: 'Quite emotional': Renowned artist's tapestries on display after 50 years
items.description: Tapestries depicting the life of Saint Francis of Assisi will be displayed together for the first time since being commissioned in the late 1960s by Australian artist Arthur Boyd.

items.title: Inquest to probe Adelaide fashion icon's death after using magic mushrooms
items.description: The death of an Adelaide fashion industry icon who suffered a cardiac arrest after taking magic mushrooms as an alternative treatment will be probed at a coronial inquest.

items.title: Family changes farm to keep Olive at home after dementia diagnosis
items.description: After Olive Eather was diagnosed with dementia, the family farmstay changed its business model to keep her at home for longer.

items.title: Bruce Lehrmann makes legal bid for Brittany Higgins documentary footage
items.description: Former Liberal staffer Bruce Lehrmann has asked a court to order the company behind a film involving Brittany Higgins to hand over raw footage.

items.title: Dockers down Cats as Bolton takes mark of the year contender
items.description: Fremantle comes from behind to beat Geelong for a 13th straight game, as Shai Bolton hits the heights at Perth Stadium with a Mark of the Year contender.

items.title: Migration dips as Coalition accuses government of failing to meet targets
items.description: Net overseas migration remained above 300,000 last year, fuelling opposition claims Labor has locked in an unsustainable new normal despite the number of arrivals continuing to fall.

items.title: Hegseth blasts NATO members, announces review of US forces in Europe
items.description: He said that too many NATO allies failed to support the US on Iran in what he called a "shameful" denial of access, basing and overflight.

items.title: Push to turn NSW south coast into state's largest national park
items.description: The National Parks Association wants an ambitious 1.2-million-hectare national park spanning from the Illawarra to the Victorian border.
